output.reason: 所提供证据直接支持肯定回答。多个片段明确报告了该综述所识别出的对滥用内容具有预测性的特征：字符n-gram（表现出对噪声、混淆和拼写错误的稳健性，且在若干数据集中效果突出——见“神经网路方法”中关于 Nobata 等和 Mehdad 与 Tetreault 的讨论），与词n-gram结合使用并配合情感词典评分等的词袋/tf-idf加权n-gram（“基于特征工程的方法”），以及分布语义特征结合手工设计特征如极性评分、LIWC 和表情符号特征（“神经网路方法”中 Samghabadi 等）。这些证据共同表明该综述确实提供了关于常见预测性特征的见解。

claims.text: Nobata et al. evaluated a large range of features on the Yahoo! datasets using a regression model: (1) word and character n-grams; (2) linguistic features such as number of polite/hate words and punctuation count; (3) syntactic features such as parent and grandparent of a node in a dependency tree; (4) distributional-semantic features such as paragraph2vec comment representations.

Although the best results were achieved with all features combined, character n-grams on their own contributed significantly more than other features due to their robustness to noise (obfuscations, misspellings, unseen words).

Mehdad and Tetreault's results demonstrated the superiority of character-level features over word-level ones, with SVM classifiers trained on Bayesian log-ratio vectors of average counts of character n-grams outperforming the approach of Nobata et al. in terms of AUC as well as other RNN-based character and word-level models.

Bag-of-words (BOW) features have been integral to several works on abuse detection; for example, Sood et al. showed that an SVM trained on word bi-gram features outperformed a word-list baseline using a Levenshtein distance-based heuristic for detecting profanity.
Word n-grams have been used in conjunction with other features, such as typed-dependency relations or scores based on sentiment lexicons, to train SVMs.
Salminen et al. showed that a linear SVM using tf-idf weighted n-grams achieves the best performance on classification of hateful comments as one of 29 different hate categories.

Samghabadi et al. augmented features with hand-engineered ones such as polarity scores derived from SentiWordNet, measures based on the LIWC program, and features based on emoticons; distributional-semantic features combined with these constituted an effective feature space.
In line with the findings of Nobata et al. and Mehdad and Tetreault, character n-grams performed well on the datasets used by Samghabadi et al.
The winning system of the GermEval shared task employed multiple character and token n-gram classifiers, as well as distributional semantic features obtained by averaging word embeddings.
The top approach for Hindi in the aggression identification shared task utilized lexical features based on word and character n-grams.
Sarcastic comments are hard for abuse detection methods to deal with since surface features are not sufficient; typically knowledge of the context or background of the user is also required.
Mishra found that metaphors are more frequent in abusive samples as opposed to non-abusive ones.
